title: 5 BIG BRAIN TRAINING TIPS TO UNFUCK YOUR PROGRAM
summary: Five programming tips NH applied while revamping his own program: drop exercises you skip anyway, build in light chances to train every muscle, use instinctive rotations within a structured plan, keep exercise selection lean and repeat what works, and let yourself swap even your main strength lift. The goal is a program fun enough to follow for years.
claims: A program should be refined constantly with small changes; a truly final program does not exist because it would have stopped evolving
Remove exercises you do not enjoy, because you end up skipping them anyway and they take the place of something you would actually do; he found one he had not done in 3 months
All-or-nothing thinking means a muscle gets skipped whenever you cannot train it hard, and the missed work piles up over a week
Build in frequent chances to train each muscle lightly; someone who trains calves lightly 40 times a year will do better than someone who trains them intensely 15 times
On every upper-body day his program includes at least one exercise for each muscle group, even if it is just a few light sets
Do not save strength for one big future session that may never come; train the muscle today while you can
Nucleus overload is a good way to give neglected small muscles more frequent work
Lifters who say they train by instinct are usually winging it; you can only improvise well once you have a well-planned program
Instinctive rotations: each upper day has 4 giant-set lines and he picks 2 or 3 of them, choosing sets per line on the day, which made training fun again
Options inside a rotation must target the same muscle in the same way, otherwise you will favour strong points and neglect weak ones
Start with scheduled biweekly rotations, then move to choosing exercises freely by how recovered you feel
You wrote the program, so do not act like a slave to it; freedom within your own structure keeps training enjoyable
Be less greedy with exercise selection: a beginner needs only one biceps exercise, such as dumbbell or EZ-bar curls, while NH, being advanced, uses 4 to 6
If an exercise works for you and rarely causes injury, repeat it constantly instead of chasing variety
Snap-grip hyperextensions hammer his hamstrings, have never injured him and recover easily, yet he rarely did them as an optional exercise; now they are programmed on every lower-body day
Whatever is inconvenient gets skipped even if it is programmed, so make key exercises convenient; he now supersets hyperextensions with Toshiki raises and does them every time
Do not be afraid to swap your main strength lift now and then, for example squats for good mornings or bench press for weighted push-ups; a week off will not cost you strength
The defining trait of a final program is that it excites you and you never dread it
The real key to hypertrophy is being able to keep training day in, day out for years, so embrace anything that helps with that
